title: refactor(ci): consolidate node workflows, improve release automation and repository hygiene
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Over time the repo accumulated multiple nearly-duplicate GitHub Actions workflows for Node-based packages (lint/test/build/release). This caused duplicated maintenance, inconsistent caching, and flaky release runs. This PR consolidates those workflows into a small set of reusable workflow templates and improves release automation hygiene (tagging, changelog generation, and safer publish steps).

Summary of changes: consolidated node lint/test/build workflows into .github/workflows/node-ci.yml and .github/workflows/release.yml; introduced reusable composite actions (.github/actions/ci-cache, .github/actions/validate-release) to centralize logic; upgraded actions to pinned versions or SHA when necessary; standardized Node version matrix (18.x, 20.x) across all jobs; fixed flaky e2e by pinning chrome-driver and increasing retry/backoff for network steps; improved cache key strategy to reduce misses; added stricter push/cancel rules to reduce duplicate release runs.

Checklist:
- [x] Consolidated duplicate workflows into shared workflows and call-sites
- [x] Replaced ad-hoc caching with composite action and consistent keys
- [x] Upgraded actions and pinned commits where security-sensitive
- [x] Added integration test retries and better logging for flaky steps
- [x] Verified that release automation runs only on protected branches and tags

Testing notes: Ran full CI across repo (lint/test/build) for Node 18/20 matrix on a feature branch; validated cache hit rates improved locally and in CI; executed a dry-run of release workflow (no publish) to validate changelog generation and tag creation; monitored action durations to ensure no regression in median runtime.

Impact and follow-ups: This reduces duplicated workflow YAML by ~60% and centralizes change points for CI behavior. Follow-ups include migrating other repos to the same composite actions, and adding observability for release runs (alerting on failed publish attempts).
commits: chore(actions): add reusable ci-cache and validate-release composite actions
fix(e2e): increase retries and pin webdriver for stable runs
chore(ci): pin critical GH Actions to SHAs and update matrix
docs(ci): update CONTRIBUTING.md with new CI workflow docs
review_comments: Liam Chen: Overall makes sense. Please explain why we kept both 18 and 20 in the matrix instead of dropping 18.
Ava Martinez: We keep 18 for backwards compatibility with some older dedicated infra customers; we'll deprecate in a follow-up once usage drops below threshold.
Priya Kaur: Suggest pinning action SHAs for security-sensitive steps (release/publish). Can you add a helper to centralize those pins?
Ava Martinez: Added ci-action-pins to the composite action and updated the release job to use pins or verified version ranges where pins are not available.
Diego Ramirez: e2e increases LGTM but please add a log line on retry count to help triage flakiness.
Ava Martinez: Added logging and bumped retry backoff to exponential with jitter.
ci_checks: release-dry-run - passed - validated changelog and tag creation
security-scan - passed - no high severity findings
ci-cache-hits - improved (observed 72% hit rate vs ~45% before)
release_notes: Consolidated Node CI workflows into a smaller, reusable set to reduce duplication and maintenance burden.
Improved release automation hygiene: safer tag creation, changelog dry-run, and pinned action SHAs for publish steps.
Stabilized flaky e2e tests by pinning webdriver and adding retries with logging.
Introduced reusable composite actions for cache and release validation to make cross-repo adoption easier.
